title: The research program
dek: Who this corpus belongs to, where the work lives, and how to read it without confusing a simulation for a spacetime theorem.
text:
Aaron Spradlin (@aaronspradlin) is Chief Technology & Security Officer at United Planners Financial Services. In parallel he runs a public AI-research ledger that asks a stubborn question without claiming the physics: if you refuse to put spacetime, a metric, or a manifold in by hand, what structure can still appear from retained information? The product he will defend is signal over hype — coherence you can audit — not Einstein.

This wiki is a compiled research area, not a census of the X account. It unifies two public streams that otherwise live in different places: the GitHub working tree proteinfoldingengine/WetLabEngine (especially Tmp/TOE) and the scientific field notes posted from @aaronspradlin. X is the archive of record. The public compile is https://aaronspradlin.grok.me. Vector search can sit on the same document units later. For now the corpus is indexed, cross-linked, and honest about claim status.

Two labs, one method

The repository root is a white-box protein-simulation audit engine: a JSON science contract, deterministic checks against raw artifacts, and an AI peer-review pass. Labs/ holds two GitHub-only coarse-grained campaigns (p53, MECP2). Nested under Tmp/TOE is a much larger geometry-from-information program — UQCF-GEM, retained atlas, holonomy, restricted-bridge theorems, cosmology derivation packets, the Great Grok Challenge validation ladder, and applied recoverability assays (batteries, SPARC rotation-curve holdouts, frozen v9 on 1UAO/1L2Y, Villin HP35, C3++ LLM telemetry).

GitHub is the source of truth for code, packages, and papers.
X is the archive of record. This wiki is a compiled index of load-bearing posts, not a dump of the account.
AI systems (Grok, Gemini Pro, Claude, OpenAI) are used as public red-team, not as oracles.
Every advertised result is supposed to be independently runnable.

Signal over hype.

What this wiki is not

It is not a claim that a Theory of Everything has been proved. Spradlin repeatedly publishes restricted theorems, numerical harnesses, and explicit “not claimed” lists. The editorial rule here matches Package 17: if a seam is open, it is labeled open.

The X and GitHub source is made available for personal, research, evaluation, and other noncommercial uses only. Commercial, product, platform, or service use requires written permission.
